title: Agentic vulnerability scanning ships at a second major vendor by Q1 2027
body: Microsoft's July 9 announcement that MDASH — its multi-model harness orchestrating more than 100 specialized AI agents to discover, debate, and prove exploitable bugs — is moving onto dedicated cloud infrastructure sized for Windows-scale scanning marks the first time an OS vendor has operationalized agentic vulnerability discovery in production. The harness has already produced hard results: 16 new vulnerabilities across the networking and authentication stack, including four critical remote-code-execution flaws in the kernel TCP/IP stack and the IKEv2 service. The prediction: within the next two to three quarters, at least one other major OS or hyperscale cloud vendor (Google, Apple, Amazon, or a Linux-ecosystem steward such as Red Hat/SUSE backed by a hyperscaler) will announce its own production-scale agentic scanning harness for a flagship codebase, and at least one of these programs will publicly tie its findings to an off-calendar, risk-driven patch release rather than a fixed monthly cycle. Three forces make this hard to avoid. First, Microsoft has explicitly framed AI-speed discovery as symmetric — the same capability works for attackers, a point underlined by the JADEPUFFER incident where an autonomous agent ran an intrusion end-to-end — so a vendor that does not scan its own code at machine speed is effectively ceding first-discovery to adversaries. Second, the raw ingredients are now commodity: this same week OpenAI shipped GPT-5.6 with a subagent-driven ultra mode and Meta opened its Muse Spark API with leading tool-use scores, meaning the multi-agent orchestration layer MDASH represents is reproducible on rented frontier models rather than requiring a bespoke research program. Third, Microsoft's public argument that calendar-bound patch cycles must give way to continuous, risk-driven remediation creates competitive and regulatory pressure on peers to show an equivalent capability. The landing zone by Q1 2027: a second vendor announcement of a production agentic scanning program, with disclosed CVE counts, and the first visible cracks in the fixed patch-Tuesday-style cadence at whichever vendors run these harnesses.

summary: Microsoft moved MDASH, its 100-agent scanning harness, into Windows-scale production, finding 16 flaws including four critical RCEs. With attackers gaining the same speed and orchestration now commodity, a second major OS or cloud vendor ships its own harness and risk-driven patching by Q1 2027.
